data.title: What KCB Group Holders Got Right
data.description:
If KCB Group sat on your watchlist instead of in your account, the outcome over the last twelve months may feel like a missed call. For KCB Group shareholders, the return over the past year was 45.7%, including dividends. That gain now sits alongside fresh Q2 2026 numbers showing higher revenue and net income than a year earlier. If you rewind to November 2025, could a simple assumption about digital adoption and African trade growth have helped you spot that potential earlier?

If the move has made KCB Group harder to judge, start where the gap is still open and scan 216 high quality undervalued stocks.

The Two Stories Investors Had To Weigh On KCB Group

The shares cost KES65 at the start of the period, and KCB Group sat between two very different stories of what might come next.

On the bullish side, one narrative pointed to aggressive digital expansion and regional trade platforms, with a Fair Value of KES94.23. This was the price implied if assumptions on 11.8% revenue growth and a future P/E of 8.3x played out.

The bearish narrative focused on geopolitical strain and fintech rivalry, with a Fair Value of KES44. This assumed 12.2% revenue growth but a lower future P/E of 3.9x because of pressure on asset quality and costs.

What The Results Changed For The KCB Group Thesis

The clearest fresh evidence came from the Q2 2026 results. Total revenue reached KSh48,581.047m versus KSh42,361.988m a year earlier, and net income moved to KSh18,257.608m from KSh15,413.821m. Net margin edged up from 36.4% to 37.6%. That combination leaned toward the optimistic KCB Group case, although it did not remove the risks in the cautious view.

The lesson to carry to other banks is simple. When a story leans on digital efficiency and scale, track whether net margin and absolute profit move together in reported results rather than relying on top-line change alone.

What KCB Group's Price Already Assumes

KCB Group now trades at KES88.5 after a 45.7% gain over the past year. The bearish analyst Narrative on Simply Wall St sets its Fair Value below that level, arguing the market already prices in a generous payoff from digital banking and regional growth.

The same Narrative focuses on whether KCB Group can scale those platforms without credit costs, regulations, and tech rivals eroding the earnings that current buyers appear to be counting on.

"Although KCB Group is investing in digital channels to widen reach, ongoing execution issues in scaling these platforms and integrating more advanced capabilities risk keeping cost to income ratios elevated and may limit the expected uplift in fee income and earnings. While regional expansion is intended to diversify revenue, continued exposure to countries with recurring conflict and hyperinflation raises the chance that future branch disruptions, higher credit losses, and regulatory hurdles could pull group revenue and net margins below what current growth plans imply."

data.title: FDA Approval Could Be A Big Moment For Regeneron Stock (REGN)
data.description:
• Regeneron Pharmaceuticals received past FDA approval for Livsayis (cemdisiran) to treat anti acetylcholine receptor antibody positive generalized myasthenia gravis in adults, based on Phase 3 NIMBLE data showing clinically meaningful gains on MG ADL and QMG scores with quarterly subcutaneous dosing.
  • This first siRNA therapy in generalized myasthenia gravis gives Regeneron a new rare disease franchise that is fully owned, siRNA based, and supported by a restricted distribution program with boxed safety warnings that may influence uptake patterns, costs, and risk management.
  • We will now see how Regeneron Pharmaceuticals' long term investment narrative could be influenced by Livsayis, which is positioned as a first in class siRNA launch.
Spot 19 high quality undiscovered gems that, like Regeneron Pharmaceuticals with Livsayis, are building under-the-radar drug pipelines focused on first-in-class therapies and genetic medicine platforms.

Regeneron Pharmaceuticals Investment Narrative Recap

To own Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, you have to believe the core franchises Dupixent and EYLEA HD, plus a wide late stage pipeline, can keep cash flows growing even as older drugs face tougher competition and pricing pressure. The analyst consensus narrative on Simply Wall St leans on that idea, with earnings forecast to rise about 10.6% a year despite slower top line growth than the broader US market.

The near term swing factor is execution on newer launches and label expansions that can offset pressure in retinal disease and any legal or reputational drag from the Libtayo melanoma lawsuits. Livsayis approval strengthens the rare disease story, but it does not change the fact that EYLEA competition and litigation remain the biggest immediate overhangs.

Among the recent updates, the European Commission decision on Libtayo dosing looks most relevant when thinking about Regeneron Pharmaceuticals around the Livsayis launch. Libtayo now offers a less frequent 700 mg every six weeks regimen after an initial period, plus shorter infusion times for some patients, which may support persistence and real world use across skin, lung and cervical cancer indications.

For investors, this feeds into the same execution question that Livsayis raises: can Regeneron convert scientific assets into durable usage in competitive markets while managing safety, boxed warnings and complex treatment logistics? If Libtayo’s more flexible schedule improves adoption or stickiness, it could soften oncology risk and give the business a little more room to absorb EYLEA pressure and fund high cost programs in obesity, siRNA and gene based therapies.

Regeneron Pharmaceuticals’ current earnings are about US$4.8b, with analysts forecasting consensus earnings of US$7.7b by 2029. That implies revenue of roughly US$23.0b and calls for around 10.8% yearly top line growth, with earnings rising by about US$2.9b over that period.

Exploring Other Perspectives

One alternate view focuses less on Livsayis and more on trial risk in the broader C5 siRNA platform. The most cautious analysts worried that a tricky transfusion avoidance endpoint in paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria could cap future rare disease earnings, which is why they were only penciling in about US$19.7b of revenue and US$6.9b of profit by 2029. Those estimates were set before the Livsayis approval. As a result, you now get a live case study in how quickly expectations and narratives can shift.

data.title: Amazon.com (AMZN) Turns $5 Billion Of AWS Data Centers Into A Leaseback Deal
data.description:
• Amazon.com (NasdaqGS:AMZN) agreed to sell a portfolio of Amazon Web Services data centers to Blackstone for US$5b in a data center REIT transaction.
  • The facilities will be leased back to AWS under a long term agreement, allowing Amazon to retain operational control of the infrastructure.
  • Blackstone plans to use the acquired sites as the seed assets for a newly formed data center REIT focused on cloud infrastructure tenants.
  • Amazon's US$5b AWS data center sale and leaseback with Blackstone is an important move to weigh against the rest of the picture. Check out 1 major warning sign that Amazon.com investors should know about.

Amazon.com now spans online retail, physical stores, subscriptions, advertising, and cloud infrastructure, so the AWS real estate footprint affects more than just servers in a warehouse. A US$2.8 trillion market cap gives the group scale to pursue capital intensive arrangements that many smaller peers cannot easily match.

4 things going right for Amazon.com that this headline doesn't cover.

How Amazon.com’s data center sale tests the “CapEx into contracts” bet

The Amazon.com Narrative hangs on a simple bargain. The group pours huge sums into AI heavy infrastructure, then relies on AWS to lock those assets into long-duration, cash-generating contracts.

"The main thing that has to go right is that Amazon.com turns its very large AI focused CapEx program, including data centers, servers and satellite infrastructure, into long duration contracts that sustain strong free cash flow and attractive returns on invested capital..."

See how the full story points towards a $331 fair value for Amazon.com.

This Blackstone deal directly speaks to that thesis. Amazon.com is effectively recycling US$5b of sunk AWS real estate into cash while keeping a long-term triple-net lease that ties those shells to committed usage. It backs the Narrative catalyst that heavy AI data center spending is supported by durable demand rather than speculative overbuilding, a point investors also weigh for Microsoft and Google parent Alphabet.

There is a trade off. The transaction also adds to the off-balance-sheet lease stack that regulators have already highlighted as a risk for AI infrastructure builders, putting pressure on the Narrative’s concern around very high CapEx and non-cash commitments. For you, the question is whether this kind of sale-and-leaseback tightens Amazon.com’s cash discipline or simply layers more fixed obligations on top of an already aggressive build.

data.title: Why Is Core Scientific (CORZ) Building A $1.3 Billion Texas Data Center?
data.description:

  • AMD is set to lease 110 MW of capacity at the site under a broader 530 MW infrastructure agreement with Core Scientific.
  • The Texas buildout would materially expand Core Scientific’s data center footprint beyond its existing bitcoin mining focused infrastructure.
  • The planned US$1.3b Texas data center and AMD’s 110 MW lease matter, but investors need to weigh other Core Scientific factors too. We have also flagged 3 warning signs (2 major) for Core Scientific.

Core Scientific operates US data centers that support high-density colocation and digital asset mining, so this Texas build points further toward catering to power hungry AI and high performance computing tenants rather than only bitcoin-focused clients.

How does the Texas project fit into Core Scientific’s shift away from Bitcoin mining?

The Quinlan build lines up with Core Scientific’s plan to exit Bitcoin mining by Q4 2026 and lean on high density AI and HPC colocation. A single US$1.3b facility oriented around tenants like AMD pushes more power capacity into contracted hosting rather than self mining, which ties future cash generation to long term service agreements.

Does this Texas move change the Core Scientific Narrative?

The news leans into the existing Narrative rather than rewriting it, because it extends the pool of contracted AI capacity beyond CoreWeave toward AMD, where 530 MW is already covered and more may follow. That supports the thesis that roughly 1.1 GW of planned AI colocation could be backed by long duration power and hosting deals, while still leaving financing and CoreWeave concentration risk in play.

What is the single biggest proof point to watch from here?

The cleanest test will be whether Core Scientific secures and discloses funding for the roughly US$6b of capital flagged for the initial AMD build, and keeps the 2026 to 2028 Quinlan construction window on track. A confirmed project financing package, paired with visible progress toward energizing the first megawatts, would show this announcement is converting into real, revenue producing capacity.

data.title: Here's Why We Think Southern Sun (JSE:SSU) Is Well Worth Watching
data.description:
It's common for many investors, especially those who are inexperienced, to buy shares in companies with a good story even if these companies are loss-making. But the reality is that when a company loses money each year, for long enough, its investors will usually take their share of those losses. Loss-making companies are always racing against time to reach financial sustainability, so investors in these companies may be taking on more risk than they should.

So if this idea of high risk and high reward doesn't suit, you might be more interested in profitable, growing companies, like Southern Sun (JSE:SSU). Even if this company is fairly valued by the market, investors would agree that generating consistent profits will continue to provide Southern Sun with the means to add long-term value to shareholders.

Trump has pledged to "unleash" American oil and gas and these 15 US stocks have developments that are poised to benefit.

Southern Sun's Earnings Per Share Are Growing

The market is a voting machine in the short term, but a weighing machine in the long term, so you'd expect share price to follow earnings per share (EPS) outcomes eventually. That makes EPS growth an attractive quality for any company. Impressively, Southern Sun has grown EPS by 23% per year, compound, in the last three years. If growth like this continues on into the future, then shareholders will have plenty to smile about.

It's often helpful to take a look at earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) margins, as well as revenue growth, to get another take on the quality of the company's growth. Not all of Southern Sun's revenue this year is revenue from operations, so keep in mind the revenue and margin numbers used in this article might not be the best representation of the underlying business. Southern Sun maintained stable EBIT margins over the last year, all while growing revenue 8.8% to R7.2b. That's a real positive.

You can take a look at the company's revenue and earnings growth trend, in the chart below. To see the actual numbers, click on the chart.

While it's always good to see growing profits, you should always remember that a weak balance sheet could come back to bite. So check Southern Sun's balance sheet strength, before getting too excited.

Are Southern Sun Insiders Aligned With All Shareholders?

It's pleasing to see company leaders with putting their money on the line, so to speak, because it increases alignment of incentives between the people running the business, and its true owners. Southern Sun followers will find comfort in knowing that insiders have a significant amount of capital that aligns their best interests with the wider shareholder group. To be specific, they have R323m worth of shares. That's a lot of money, and no small incentive to work hard. While their ownership only accounts for 2.2%, this is still a considerable amount at stake to encourage the business to maintain a strategy that will deliver value to shareholders.

Does Southern Sun Deserve A Spot On Your Watchlist?

You can't deny that Southern Sun has grown its earnings per share at a very impressive rate. That's attractive. Further, the high level of insider ownership is impressive and suggests that the management appreciates the EPS growth and has faith in Southern Sun's continuing strength. Fast growth and confident insiders should be enough to warrant further research, so it would seem that it's a good stock to follow.
